title: Console walkthrough - usage analytics & cost breakdown
next_steps: Alex to send pricing and seat vs usage options
Priya to share dashboard export and routing policy doc
Solis to provide 1-week sample traffic for pilot
Schedule pilot kickoff for week of 2026-03-09
action_items: Alex Chen: Send tailored pricing + seat-based vs usage options (due 2026-03-09)
Priya Kapoor: Share sample dashboard export + routing policy doc (due 2026-03-06)
Sara Gomez: Upload 1-week sample request logs to Redwood S3 bucket / share link (due 2026-03-11)
Lena Ortiz: Confirm compliance checklist items and ask for SOC2 docs (due 2026-03-08)
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. I'm Alex from Redwood, AE on the account. Priya and Jon are here from our solutions/SE side. How are you all?
[00:08] Mark Ellis: Doing good, thanks. Excited to see the console details.
[00:12] Priya Kapoor: Awesome, we'll keep this pretty focused on usage analytics and per-route cost so you can see where dollars come from and how to optimize. Quick agenda: overview of dashboards, demo per-route panels, cost breakdown, then Q&A and next steps.
[00:28] Tom Reeves: Sounds good, I'm mainly interested in ops visibility — latencies per route and cost attribution.
[00:33] Priya Kapoor: Great, that's exactly what we'll cover. One note, transcription is a bit fuzzy sometimes so names might show up weirdly on the recording.
[00:39] Jon Park: Jumping in, I'm going to share the console — bear with the screen share.
[00:45] [screen share begins]
[00:50] Priya Kapoor: Ok first panel is 'Overview' — total tokens, requests, 99 P95 latencies, error rate, and cost trend by day. This view aggregates across models and routes.
[01:05] Mark Ellis: Are those token counts per call or aggregated? Looks like aggregated.
[01:09] Priya Kapoor: Aggregated. You can toggle to per-route aggregation which is the key part — we'll switch now to a route view for your storefront suggestion route.
[01:17] [00:01:30] Alex Chen: A couple quick qualifiers — Hosted vs Dedicated will show different baselines for cost. We group cost into compute, model licensing (if any), and auxiliary (network, storage). For you right now, hosted usage is the starting point.
[01:33] Sara Gomez: On compute, is that per-token or per-inference? Our team usually reasons in per-token for chat but per-request for embeddings.
[01:40] Priya Kapoor: Good question. We break it down both ways. The console shows per-token unit cost and also per-request median cost. For chat routes with streaming you'll see token cost and network egress.
[01:53] [00:02:05] Priya Kapoor: Switching to 'Per-route dashboards' — here you get a panel per API route (e.g., /generate-storefront, /search-embed). Each panel shows: volume over time, latency histogram, cost by token vs overhead, top prompt templates, and failure reasons.
[02:10] Mark Ellis: Top prompt templates — can you map that back to our internal prompt IDs?
[02:14] Priya Kapoor: Yes, we let you attach metadata to requests (route tags or prompt_id) so the dashboard shows human-friendly names. If you don't supply IDs we attempt to cluster similar payloads but it is less precise.
[02:25] Tom Reeves: If we wanted to split routing by latency SLO — like send high-priority users to dedicated — can we see the cost impact before committing?
[02:31] Jon Park: You can create a simulated routing policy in the console and run a 'what-if' analysis. It will estimate cost and latency percentiles based on historical traffic patterns and model variants.
[02:42] [00:03:10] Sara Gomez: Nice. How accurate are those estimates when we use quantized model variants?
[03:17] Priya Kapoor: We account for quantization profiles — we have baseline performance profiles for each variant in the catalog. If you use a custom quantized build in Private, we'd recommend running a short benchmark with the same sequence length distribution. The simulator will flag variance.
[03:34] Mark Ellis: Security question — are these dashboards multi-tenant within an org? We need RBAC so ops sees infra metrics and ML sees prompt-level stuff but not customer PII.
[03:44] Alex Chen: Yes, RBAC is supported. We also redact payload contents unless you opt-in. For Private we can hook into your KMS and audit logs flow. Lena, I know you'll want the compliance packet — we'll send SOC2/ISO artifacts.
[03:58] Lena Ortiz: Please do, and also sample audit log format.
[04:02] [00:04:10] Priya Kapoor: Back to cost breakdown — here's the per-route cost table. For /generate-storefront we show average tokens per request 420, avg latency 320ms, cost per request $0.023, cost per token $0.000055. You can click 'drill into day' to see outliers.
[04:23] Tom Reeves: That per-request number — does that include cache savings? We do some prefix caching on our side.
[04:28] Priya Kapoor: If caching happens through Redwood (prefix/KV caching) we surface the effective cost after cache hits. If it's external caching you can post metadata about cache-hit vs miss and we'll visualize it but it won't be automatic.
[04:39] [00:04:50] Alex Chen: Also note we annotate spikes — if a route suddenly doubles tokens per request the console highlights correlation with model rollouts, code deploys, or prompt changes if you tag them.
[05:00] Sara Gomez: Is there an exportable CSV of the per-route breakdown? We need to drop it into our finance models.
[05:06] Jon Park: Yes, every table has an 'export' button and you can schedule daily exports to an S3 bucket or Slack.
[05:12] [00:05:40] Mark Ellis: How about alerting — can we set cost thresholds per route?
[05:17] Priya Kapoor: Absolutely. We have per-route alerting on spend, token rate, and latency SLOs. Alerts can trigger Slack, PagerDuty, or webhook.
[05:25] Tom Reeves: Great. For our pilot we'd likely do 3 routes — storefront generate, product Q&A, and search embed — and want to limit cost exposure.
[05:33] Alex Chen: Makes sense. We'll suggest a routing policy: high-value users -> dedicated low-latency variant; bulk batch jobs -> cheaper quantized chunk with async responses. The console shows estimated monthly cost for that policy.
[05:47] [00:06:10] Sara Gomez: I saw earlier a 'model delta' visualization — that shows quality regressions after model change?
[06:15] Priya Kapoor: Yes, under Optimize we track evals and a set of labeled prompts. You can tie regressions to route performance by linking the prompt set to a route. If quality drops we can auto-fallback to previous model for affected routes.
[06:29] Mark Ellis: Does fallback increase cost significantly? If we fallback to a larger hosted model, cost could spike.
[06:35] Alex Chen: That's where the rollback policy is important — you can set an automatic fallback to a cheaper but still-compatible variant, or page your on-call. The console will show the estimated delta cost for the rollback action.
[06:48] [00:06:50] Tom Reeves: For billing granularity, we need to show per-team chargebacks — can we tag routes with team ownership?
[06:58] Priya Kapoor: Yep, tags are first-class. You can group by tag in the cost view and generate per-tag spend for finance.
[07:05] Sara Gomez: A couple of nitty-gritty: sequence length distribution — where do we see that?
[07:10] Jon Park: Under route diagnostics, there's a histogram of sequence lengths and tokenization breakdown. This feeds into our kernel selection estimator so recommendations are workload-aware.
[07:22] [00:07:30] Mark Ellis: Let's talk pilot size and timeline. We're thinking a two-week pilot with shadow routing for the three routes. What's realistic?
[07:39] Alex Chen: Two weeks sounds fine for a smoke and cost/latency assessment. For the bench we'd need your sample traffic logs and an S3 bucket to export results. Priya can run a simulated run and a small live pilot.
[07:51] Sara Gomez: We can anonymize logs and share. We'll need instructions on the format.
[07:55] Priya Kapoor: I'll share the schema — request_id, route, prompt_id, approx seq_length, user_tag. If you can include timing distribution that's ideal.
[08:06] [00:08:20] Lena Ortiz: For Private deployment questions, can the console run on a private control plane? We need to ensure telemetry doesn't flow to public Redwood.
[08:14] Alex Chen: Yes, Private has a customer-managed control plane option. Telemetry can be ingested into your VPC and storage stays on-prem or in your cloud. We'll include the architecture doc.
[08:26] Tom Reeves: Any gotchas with on-prem GPUs and quantization?
[08:29] Priya Kapoor: Your infra team should ensure CUDA/cuDNN compatibility with our runtime. Quantization works but kernel performance can vary — that's why we advise a quick benchmark.
[08:39] [00:08:50] Mark Ellis: Competitor question — some vendors do per-model flat fees which can be simpler. How do you compare?
[08:47] Alex Chen: We can do reserved capacity contracts (Reserved/Dedicated) which mimic flat costs with commit discounts. The console supports hybrid billing attribution so you can see effective unit economics.
[08:59] Sara Gomez: Nice. I noticed a spike in the demo data around minute 24 — what was that?
[09:05] Jon Park: That was simulated burst traffic tied to a synthetic campaign. The console highlights correlated deploys and gives likely causes but not perfect detection.
[09:14] [00:09:40] Priya Kapoor: Quick demo of 'what changed' — click a spike and the console will show top changes in payload size, model version, and request sources. You can then jump to a list of sample requests (redacted) to inspect.
[09:29] Tom Reeves: Can we integrate with our internal APM for trace correlation?
[09:33] Priya Kapoor: Yes, we have trace hooks and can ingest trace IDs. We also support OpenTelemetry and emit spans back to your APM.
[09:40] Mark Ellis: Ok this is helpful, especially the per-route spend and tag-based chargeback.
[09:44] [00:10:10] Alex Chen: Recap and next steps: we'll send the pricing and pilot proposal; Priya will share the dashboard export and data schema; you will provide anonymized logs; Lena will confirm compliance ask list. We'll aim for pilot kickoff next week pending logs.
[10:00] Sara Gomez: Sounds good. A couple of lingering Qs: how do we handle model rollouts during pilot to avoid false positives in evals?
[10:07] Priya Kapoor: For the pilot we'd pin model versions per route. If you enable rollouts we suggest canaries on small percentage and auto-fallback thresholds. We'll show you the UI for that.
[10:18] Tom Reeves: Any limits on historical retention for the analytics?
[10:21] Jon Park: Hosted default is 90 days for detailed logs with aggregated metrics for 13 months. We can extend retention as an addon.
[10:30] [00:10:50] Lena Ortiz: For SOC2 documents, will that be a full package or summary?
[10:34] Alex Chen: We'll send the standard compliance pack and a redacted sample audit log. For Private customers we provide more granular artifacts.
[10:44] Sara Gomez: Ok thanks — I'm going to circle with my finance partner on projected spend for the three-route pilot.
[10:50] Alex Chen: Great — we'll include estimated monthly cost with a few routing scenarios in the proposal.
[10:57] [00:11:20] Mark Ellis: Last quick thing — do you support per-token throttles? We want to limit cost per user.
[11:03] Priya Kapoor: Yes, rate limits and per-user quotas are configurable. You can set enforcement on the edge or in the Redwood runtime.
[11:11] Tom Reeves: Perfect.
[11:13] Alex Chen: Alright if there's nothing else we'll wrap. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts and a proposed pilot schedule.
[11:21] Sara Gomez: Thanks all.
[11:23] Lena Ortiz: Thanks.
[11:25] [00:11:45] [meeting ends]

Notes on transcription: slight mis-hear on a couple of names; timestamps approximate. The call lasted ~42 minutes and included a live console demo, simulated traffic spike analysis, and agreement to kick off a two-week pilot once Solis provides anonymized request logs.
